sounds.name: Disco Toms
sounds.ref: In the style of the late-1970s disco synth tom
sounds.blurb: Two tuned toms that fall in pitch as they ring, the “pew” of a 1979 dance record.
sounds.how: Each channel is one oscillator struck by a key and sweeping down from where it is struck. A falling pitch over a third of a second is what the ear hears as a synth tom rather than a note. Channel 2 is tuned higher, so the fill moves between two drums.

steps.title: One oscillator, tuned low
steps.why:
OSC MODE starts at A, one oscillator, the classic drum-synth sound. TUNE sets the pitch the drum is struck at.
- Channel 1 TUNE 3.5 (177 Hz): a floor tom. The keys below middle C strike channel 1 at this pitch whichever key you press.
- Listen for: a short, dull knock. It is still a click of a drum; the next steps give it length and its fall.

steps.title: Let it ring
steps.why:
DECAY sets how long the drum rings, and the same decay closes the filter as it fades.
- Channel 1 DECAY 6.5 (300 ms): long enough to hear the pitch move.
- Channel 1 WIDTH 3 (1.8 oct): the strike opens the filter almost two octaves above TUNE and it falls back as the drum dies, a soft attack rather than a crack.
- Listen for: a round tone with a little brightness at the front. Play some keys softly: a gentle hit is quieter and duller, as on a pad.

steps.title: The falling sweep
steps.why:
SWEEP is already DOWN: every strike starts at TUNE and slides down by RANGE at SPEED. This fall is the sound of the Syncussion.
- Channel 1 SWEEP SPEED 4 (360 ms): the time the fall takes. Slower is a lazy “peeew”, faster a thump.
- Channel 1 SWEEP RANGE 3.5 (+12.6 st): a fall of just over an octave.
- Listen for: each hit dropping in pitch as it fades. Set SWEEP to OFF and the tom turns into a plain knock.

steps.title: A second, higher tom
steps.why:
Channel 2 is a whole second drum, played from middle C up. Set it like channel 1, a little higher.
- Channel 2 TUNE 5 (330 Hz), DECAY 6 (220 ms), WIDTH 3 (1.8 oct): a rack tom, a little shorter.
- Channel 2 SWEEP SPEED 4 (360 ms), RANGE 3.5 (+12.6 st): the same fall.
- Listen for: the fill moving between a low and a high tom.

context.ch1.sweepRange: In this sound: how far each tom falls. More is a deeper “pew”.
context.ch1.tune: In this sound: the pitch of the low tom.

tweaks.hear: From a long, lazy fall to a short thump.
The toms rise instead of fall, an odd, questioning sound.

sounds.name: Laser Zap
sounds.ref: In the style of the space-disco laser shot
sounds.blurb: A high strike that dives three octaves, the ray-gun effect of late-1970s dance floors.
sounds.how: The pitch starts high and the sweep drags it down a long way, slowly enough to follow. With little filter movement the tone stays pure, so the ear hears a falling whistle rather than a drum.

steps.title: Strike it high
steps.why:
A laser starts where a tom would be a bell.
- Channel 2 TUNE 9 (1.7 kHz): high and piercing.
- Listen for: a short high ping on the keys from middle C up.

steps.title: A long, deep dive
steps.why:
SWEEP is DOWN. Make the fall long and wide.
- Channel 2 SWEEP RANGE 10 (+36 st): three octaves, the whole range.
- Channel 2 SWEEP SPEED 3 (590 ms): slow enough to hear the whole dive.
- Listen for: a “pyeeew” falling right down.

steps.title: Let it ring, keep it pure
steps.why:
DECAY has to outlast the dive, and a narrow WIDTH keeps the tone a clean whistle.
- Channel 2 DECAY 7.5 (550 ms): the shot rings through its fall.
- Channel 2 WIDTH 2 (1.2 oct): only a little brightness on the strike.
- Listen for: the full laser. Raise WIDTH and it gains a harsher, buzzier edge.

context.ch2.sweepRange: In this sound: how far the laser dives.
context.ch2.sweepSpeed: In this sound: how long the dive takes.

tweaks.hear: From a slow, sinking siren to a quick zap.
A rising blip, the sound of a power-up.

sounds.name: Metal Bell
sounds.blurb: A clangorous struck bell, the inharmonic ring of one oscillator bending another.
sounds.how: In mode B oscillator 1 is not heard: it bends the pitch of oscillator 2 hundreds of times a second (frequency modulation). That adds partials that do not line up with the pitch, which the ear hears as metal. A long decay and no sweep let it ring like a bell.

steps.title: Switch to FM
steps.why:
OSC MODE B: oscillator 1 frequency-modulates oscillator 2, and only oscillator 2 is heard.
- Channel 2 OSC MODE B: the tone turns hard and metallic at once.
- Channel 2 TUNE 6 (500 Hz): a mid bell.
- Listen for: a clang instead of a knock. Turn OSC MODE back to A to hear the plain oscillator again.

steps.title: Hold the pitch
steps.why:
A bell does not fall in pitch, so turn the sweep off.
- Channel 2 SWEEP OFF.
- Listen for: a steady, ringing pitch.

steps.title: Let it ring bright
steps.why:
- Channel 2 DECAY 8.5 (1.0 s): a full second of ring.
- Channel 2 WIDTH 5 (3.0 oct): the strike opens the filter three octaves, so the clang is bright, then mellows as it dies.
- Listen for: the brightness fading while the bell keeps ringing. The soft hit in the riff is darker as well as quieter.

context.ch2.mode: In this sound: B, the FM mode that makes it metallic.
context.ch2.width: In this sound: how bright the bell is when struck.

tweaks.hear: The bell changes character, not just pitch: the clashing partials move against each other.
Noise joins the FM, like a struck sheet of thin metal.

sounds.name: Two-Channel Snare
sounds.ref: In the style of the 808-style snare the Syncussion makes from both channels
sounds.blurb: A snare built from two drums struck together: a tuned body on channel 1 and a burst of noise on channel 2.
sounds.how: A real snare is a drum skin and a rattle of wires. Here channel 1 is the skin, one oscillator with a quick pitch drop, and channel 2 in mode F is the wires, filtered noise. Struck together, from two keys at once, they read as one drum.

steps.title: The body: a short, tuned knock
steps.why:
Channel 1 is the drum skin.
- Channel 1 TUNE 4.5 (268 Hz): the snare’s note.
- Channel 1 DECAY 4.5 (91 ms): short, a knock not a tom.
- Listen for: a woody tock on the keys below middle C.

steps.title: A quick drop on the body
steps.why:
A fast, small sweep gives the skin its snap.
- Channel 1 SWEEP SPEED 7 (85 ms), RANGE 2 (+7.2 st): a fifth down, very fast.
- Listen for: a tighter, punchier tock.

steps.title: The wires: noise on channel 2
steps.why:
OSC MODE F is noise alone. TUNE still sets the filter, so here it sets the noise’s colour.
- Channel 2 OSC MODE F.
- Channel 2 TUNE 7.5 (932 Hz): the filter sits about an octave above that, a mid hiss.
- Channel 2 WIDTH 6 (3.6 oct) and DECAY 5 (120 ms): a bright burst that dies quickly.
- Listen for: the two together on each beat. The riff strikes both channels at once, a key below middle C and one above.

context.ch2.mode: In this sound: F, noise only, the snare wires.
context.ch1.decay: In this sound: the length of the drum body.

tweaks.hear: From a tight electro snare to a long, washy one.
Less rattle, more of the tuned body: a rimshot rather than a snare.

sounds.name: Robot Chatter
sounds.ref: The random-bleep sound of late-1970s sci-fi
sounds.blurb: A metallic voice that jumps to a new random pitch a dozen times a second while it rings.
sounds.how: The sample and hold picks a random pitch at the LFO speed and holds it until the next one. Over a struck FM tone with a long decay it sounds like a machine talking to itself. It works with the LFO wave switched off, because it uses only the LFO’s speed.

steps.title: A ringing FM tone
steps.why:
- Channel 1 OSC MODE B: the metallic FM mode.
- Channel 1 TUNE 5.5 (406 Hz).
- Channel 1 SWEEP OFF, so the pitch only moves where the sample and hold puts it.
- Listen for: a steady clang below middle C.

steps.title: Ring long enough to talk
steps.why:
- Channel 1 DECAY 7 (410 ms).
- Listen for: each hit ringing on through the beat.

steps.title: Switch on the sample and hold
steps.why:
S/H takes a new random pitch at LFO SPEED, by up to LFO DEPTH. The LFO WAVE switch stays OFF.
- Channel 1 S/H ON.
- Channel 1 LFO SPEED 7 (12 Hz): twelve new pitches a second.
- Channel 1 LFO DEPTH 6 (+4.3 st): up to a third either way.
- Listen for: the chatter. Slow the LFO SPEED right down and it becomes a random melody instead.

context.ch1.sh: In this sound: on, the random pitch steps.
context.ch1.lfoSpeed: In this sound: how fast the robot chatters.

tweaks.hear: From a nervous flutter to wild leaps across an octave.
The LFO’s trill adds to the random steps.

sounds.name: Struck Harder
sounds.blurb: A two-tone drum whose pitch bend follows how hard each hit is, soft hits low and hard hits swooping.
sounds.how: Mode D mixes both oscillators and replaces the sweep with the strike itself: oscillator 1 bends by as much as the hit is hard, and oscillator 2 bends with the decay. Played with soft and hard notes, one drum gives a whole range of sounds, as it did from the pads.

steps.title: Switch to mode D
steps.why:
OSC MODE D mixes the two oscillators, and the SWEEP faders no longer do anything: the hit sets the sweep.
- Channel 1 OSC MODE D.
- Channel 1 TUNE 4 (217 Hz).
- Listen for: two tones, slightly apart, swooping up into pitch as they are struck.

steps.title: Give the hits room
steps.why:
- Channel 1 DECAY 6.5 (300 ms).
- Channel 1 WIDTH 5 (3.0 oct): hard hits are brighter as well as louder, because the hit also sets how far the decay opens the filter.
- Listen for: the riff’s soft and hard notes. Soft ones are quiet thuds; the hard ones on the beat swoop and crack.

context.ch1.mode: In this sound: D, where how hard you hit sets the sweep.

tweaks.hear: The swoop keeps its shape at any pitch, from a deep boom to a tight ping.
